item.content:encoded:
A zine festival is coming to Pensacola, with HalloZine Fest 2026 set to kick off Thursday, according to a social media post. The event will celebrate independent publishing and zine culture in the area.

Zines—self-published magazines and booklets—have long been a cornerstone of DIY creative communities, and the festival aims to bring together local and regional artists, writers, and publishers. The event typically features vendor booths, workshops, and opportunities for fans and creators to connect over the independent publishing scene.

More details about the festival's specific location, times, and featured vendors were not immediately available. Listeners interested in attending can search for HalloZine Fest 2026 on social media or local event listings for additional information.

The charges represent serious felonies involving exploitation of minors and animals. The FDLE investigation led to the arrest and charges against the former officer, who is no longer employed by PPD.

Details regarding the specific circumstances of the investigation, the number of charges, and any additional information about the officer's tenure with the department were not immediately available. The case remains under investigation.

item.title: Shumaker Advisors launches roundtable series with Amendment 3 discussion
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Shumaker Advisors is launching The Connection Point, a new roundtable series aimed at bringing together business, civic, and government leaders across Northwest Florida for discussions on regional opportunities and challenges. The inaugural event, held in partnership with the Greater Pensacola Chamber of Commerce, will focus on Amendment 3. The…
item.content:encoded:
Shumaker Advisors is launching The Connection Point, a new roundtable series aimed at bringing together business, civic, and government leaders across Northwest Florida for discussions on regional opportunities and challenges.

The inaugural event, held in partnership with the Greater Pensacola Chamber of Commerce, will focus on Amendment 3. The roundtable is scheduled for Thursday, October 29, 2026, at 1 p.m., and will be led by Escambia County Commissioner Mike Kohler and Walter Pierce. According to a press release, the discussion will examine the amendment from multiple perspectives to help attendees understand the issue and its potential implications.

Sara Lefevers, Vice President at Shumaker Advisors, said the series is designed to create "a trusted space" for regional leaders to exchange ideas on complex issues and identify collaboration opportunities. "Northwest Florida's continued success depends on leaders from across the region having a trusted space to exchange ideas, better understand complex issues, and identify opportunities to work together," Lefevers said in the release.

The firm plans to announce additional roundtables and topics as the series continues. Those interested can register for the inaugural event through Shumaker Advisors.

Among the funded projects are a new doula program to support mothers during pregnancy and postpartum, funding for a full-time developmental pediatrician to serve young children with…
item.content:encoded:
The Escambia Children's Trust has distributed $3,639,575 in Bright Beginnings grants to support early childhood development and family services across the county.

Among the funded projects are a new doula program to support mothers during pregnancy and postpartum, funding for a full-time developmental pediatrician to serve young children with developmental concerns, and expanded services reaching into the Century and North Escambia County areas that have historically had fewer resources.

In total, 11 different projects were selected to receive funding through the competitive grant process. The awards reflect the trust's focus on giving young children in Escambia County a strong start through evidence-based programs and increased access to specialized care.

item.content:encoded: Pensacola and North Escambia are in for a stretch of pleasant fall weather over the next few days, with mostly sunny skies and warm afternoons expected through Friday. Residents should enjoy the dry weather window while it lasts and keep an eye on weekend forecasts for timing and intensity of potential precipitation.

item.title: AAA warns of Halloween road dangers Saturday night in Pensacola area
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: With Halloween falling on Saturday this year, the Auto Club Group is urging Pensacola-area drivers and families to exercise extra caution as neighborhoods fill with trick-or-treaters, weekend motorists, and riders on bikes and e-scooters after dark. According to AAA spokesman Mark Jenkins, the combination of increased foot traffic and weekend…
item.content:encoded:
With Halloween falling on Saturday this year, the Auto Club Group is urging Pensacola-area drivers and families to exercise extra caution as neighborhoods fill with trick-or-treaters, weekend motorists, and riders on bikes and e-scooters after dark.

According to AAA spokesman Mark Jenkins, the combination of increased foot traffic and weekend driving activity creates a particularly risky scenario. Safe Kids Worldwide reports that children are more than twice as likely to be struck and killed by a vehicle on Halloween than any other day of the year. Peak trick-or-treating hours—5:30 to 9:30 p.m.—coincide with darkness, compounding the hazard. Adding another layer of concern, federal data shows 201 people died in alcohol-related crashes on Halloween nights between 2020 and 2024.

AAA recommends drivers slow down in neighborhoods, eliminate distractions, and actively watch for pedestrians and cyclists. The organization also advises trick-or-treaters to wear reflective materials, carry flashlights, use crosswalks, and avoid stepping between parked cars. Parents should supervise children under 12 and ensure costumes don't obstruct vision or movement.

"Expect more people to be out after dark and slow down in neighborhoods," Jenkins said. "A child in a costume, or someone riding an e-bike or e-scooter, can appear in your path with very little warning."

item.content:encoded:
The Trump Administration has approved a Major Disaster Declaration for Florida in the wake of Hurricane Isaias, which struck the state earlier this month, according to reporting from WKRG News 5.

The declaration makes federal Emergency Management Agency assistance available to a dozen Florida counties dealing with storm damage. While the report references comments from Pensacola Mayor D.C., the full details of which specific counties are included and the scope of available assistance were not fully detailed in the available reporting.

Major Disaster Declarations typically unlock various forms of federal aid, including grants for temporary housing, home repairs, and low-interest disaster loans for both individuals and businesses affected by the storm. The declaration comes as recovery efforts continue across the affected areas.

item.title: Democratic CFO candidate Taddeo joins Jolly-Graham tour stops in Jacksonville, Gainesville
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Democratic candidate for Florida Chief Financial Officer Annette Taddeo will campaign Wednesday alongside gubernatorial and lieutenant gubernatorial candidates David Jolly and Gwen Graham as part of their Believe in Better Tour, with stops planned in Jacksonville and Gainesville ahead of Election Day. The Jacksonville rally begins at 2 p.m.…
item.content:encoded:
Democratic candidate for Florida Chief Financial Officer Annette Taddeo will campaign Wednesday alongside gubernatorial and lieutenant gubernatorial candidates David Jolly and Gwen Graham as part of their Believe in Better Tour, with stops planned in Jacksonville and Gainesville ahead of Election Day.

The Jacksonville rally begins at 2 p.m. Wednesday at the International Longshoremen's Association hall on East 21st Street and will also feature Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Angie Nixon. That evening, Taddeo, Jolly, and Graham will hold a get-out-the-vote rally in Gainesville at the Woman's Club on University Avenue starting at 6 p.m.

Taddeo, a former state senator and small business owner, is running on a platform centered on affordability, accountability, and anti-corruption. According to her campaign, she aims to lower costs for Floridians, protect consumers, and combat government waste and corruption if elected to the statewide fiscal office. Media interested in covering either event can contact Ulysses del Pino at 786-527-0144.

item.title: Sen. Moody Secures $11M Federal Grant for Port of Fernandina Infrastructure
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Senator Ashley Moody has helped the Ocean Highway and Port Authority land an $11 million federal grant to address flooding and structural damage at the Port of Fernandina, according to a press release issued today. The Port Infrastructure Development Program funding will support flood mitigation and dock rehabilitation projects, including drainage…
item.content:encoded:
Senator Ashley Moody has helped the Ocean Highway and Port Authority land an $11 million federal grant to address flooding and structural damage at the Port of Fernandina, according to a press release issued today.

The Port Infrastructure Development Program funding will support flood mitigation and dock rehabilitation projects, including drainage system upgrades, water capture infrastructure, pumps for surge and rainfall events, crane rail repair, and structural reinforcement. The port has faced chronic flooding and deterioration that threatened its operational capacity and worker safety.

"Florida's ports are critical to our economy, supporting thousands of jobs and helping businesses move goods across the country and around the world," Moody said in a statement. The Port of Fernandina, located on the Amelia River, supports more than 4,600 jobs and generates nearly $1.3 billion in annual economic contributions to Northeast Florida, according to port authority data.

Moody had previously urged the U.S. Department of Transportation to approve the funding request in a June letter to Maritime Administration Administrator Captain Stephen Carmel. Congressman Aaron Bean (FL-04) also backed the grant, calling the port "a small but mighty, strategically vital, and irreplaceable asset" for the region's supply chain.

item.title: Fall Fun Across Santa Rosa County: Pumpkin Patches, Markets, and Car Show This Weekend
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County is packed with family-friendly activities this fall, with several events hitting their peak season through November and a couple of standout options this coming weekend. If you're looking for Halloween festivities, the 26th Annual Navarre Beach Autorama takes place Saturday, October 31st at Navarre High School, featuring over 150…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County is packed with family-friendly activities this fall, with several events hitting their peak season through November and a couple of standout options this coming weekend.

If you're looking for Halloween festivities, the 26th Annual Navarre Beach Autorama takes place Saturday, October 31st at Navarre High School, featuring over 150 classic and vintage cars, trucks, and bikes. The show runs from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., with music, food, and vendor booths. Check-in starts at 8, and judging begins at 11 a.m. That same morning, the Navarre Beach Sea Turtle Conservation Center is hosting a Halloween-themed Trash Bash from 8 to 10 a.m., encouraging volunteers in upcycled or marine-themed costumes to help clean up and protect sea turtles and other wildlife.

For ongoing fall activities, two major pumpkin patches are in full swing. Holland Farms Pumpkin Patch & Maze in Milton offers hayrides, train rides, a corn maze, zip lines, and an eight-acre corn maze, along with free boiled peanuts for every visitor. Sweet Season Farms, also in Milton, features its 18th annual corn maze plus u-pick pumpkins and sunflowers, with over 25 farm activities and a bakery serving caramel apples and kettle corn. Both are open daily through early November.

If you prefer shopping and dining, the Highway 87 Outdoor Market in Navarre sets up the first and third Saturday of each month with farm-to-table vendors and local crafts, while Sand Dollar Plaza in Navarre hosts community appreciation events every Saturday. For more details on any of these events, visit the Santa Rosa County tourism website or contact individual venues directly.
